title: Digital India 2026: 67 Cr DigiLocker, UMANG, BharatNet, UPI Stats
meta_description: Digital India: DigiLocker 67 Cr users, UMANG 10.51 Cr, BharatNet 2.18 L villages, UPI handles 49% of global real-time payments. Citizen services free.

hero.one_liner: India's flagship digital transformation programme - DigiLocker, UMANG, BharatNet, UPI, BHASHINI and more, transforming 2.18 lakh Gram Panchayats into digital villages

what_is_it: Digital India is the Government of India's flagship programme to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. Launched on 1 July 2015 by PM Modi, it operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and is built around nine strategic pillars covering broadband connectivity, e-governance, e-services, digital literacy, electronics manufacturing, and IT for jobs.

Digital India is not a single scheme but an umbrella programme covering several flagship initiatives: DigiLocker (digital document wallet, 67 crore users, 967 crore documents issued), UMANG (unified citizen services app, 10.51 crore users, 2,446 services in 23 languages), BharatNet (rural broadband, 2.18 lakh Gram Panchayats connected by 6.92 lakh km of optical fibre), UPI (handled 49% of global real-time digital transactions in 2023), BHASHINI (AI-powered translation across 35+ Indian languages), and Common Service Centres (last-mile e-governance access points).

By 2026, Digital India is in its 11th year of operation and continues to be the foundation of India's digital public infrastructure (DPI). India is now globally recognised for its UPI-led real-time payments, Aadhaar-based identity, and DigiLocker-powered document verification - together known as the "India Stack." PMGDISHA (Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan), the digital literacy component, concluded on 31 March 2024 after training 6.39 crore people, exceeding its 6 crore target.

extra_sections.heading: The Five Most Useful Digital India Platforms
content: Most citizens benefit from Digital India through five flagship platforms - all free and accessible to every Indian:

DigiLocker: Store and access your Aadhaar, PAN, driving licence, vehicle RC, 10th and 12th certificates, COVID vaccination certificate, and many more government-issued documents - all in one digital wallet. Linked to Aadhaar for instant verification, accepted as legally valid proof. As of late 2025, 67 crore users have issued and downloaded 967 crore documents.

UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance): A single mobile app offering 2,446 government services across 3,543 schemes from central, state, and local governments. EPFO balance check, Aadhaar update, PAN application, passport status, gas booking, electricity bill payment - all in one app, in 23 Indian languages.

BharatNet: The world's largest rural broadband project, bringing high-speed internet via 6.92 lakh km of optical fibre to 2.18 lakh Gram Panchayats. This makes online education, telemedicine, e-governance, and digital commerce possible in villages.

UPI (Unified Payments Interface): The world's most successful real-time payment system, handling 1,867+ crore transactions worth ₹24.77 lakh crore in April 2025 alone. 460 million users, 65 million merchants. UPI is now live in 7+ countries including UAE, Singapore, France, and Sri Lanka.

BHASHINI: AI-powered translation platform breaking language barriers. Supports 35+ Indian languages with 1,600+ AI models. Integrated into IRCTC for railway booking, NPCI for IVRS, and police documentation. 18 language services covering speech-to-text, text-to-speech, translation, OCR, and language detection.

extra_sections.heading: The 9 Pillars of Digital India
content: The Digital India programme is structured around 9 strategic pillars, each addressing a specific aspect of digital transformation:
1. Broadband Highways: High-capacity fibre networks via BharatNet for rural and urban areas.
2. Universal Access to Mobile Connectivity: Mobile coverage in uncovered areas, especially remote and Naxal-affected regions.
3. Public Internet Access Programme: Common Service Centres (CSCs) and post offices as multi-service centres.
4. e-Governance: Reforming government through technology - paperless, presence-less, cashless service delivery.
5. eKranti - Electronic Delivery of Services: E-Education, E-Health, E-Agriculture, E-Justice, E-Security.
6. Information for All: MyGov platform, open data portals, social media engagement.
7. Electronics Manufacturing: Make in India for electronics, India Semiconductor Mission (₹76,000 crore), Indian-made chips.
8. IT for Jobs: Training in IT/ITES across smaller towns and cities; BPO incentives for tier-2/3 cities.
9. Early Harvest Programmes: Wi-Fi in universities, biometric attendance, secure email, e-Greetings.

extra_sections.title: All Digital India services are free for citizens
extra_sections.content: DigiLocker, UMANG, UPI, BHASHINI, BharatNet last-mile access - all are free for individual citizens to use. Some services on UMANG (like LPG booking) may charge the underlying service fee, but the platform itself is free. If anyone - agent, middleman, or app - charges you to "register for UMANG" or "activate DigiLocker," it is a scam. Download UMANG and DigiLocker directly from Google Play Store or Apple App Store.

extra_sections.heading: How Digital India Affects Daily Life
content: Beyond the headline numbers, Digital India has changed everyday life in India in tangible ways:

Document storage and verification: You no longer need to carry physical copies of Aadhaar, driving licence, or vehicle RC. Show the DigiLocker version on your phone - accepted by traffic police, banks, schools, hospitals.

Government services without travel: EPF balance check, Aadhaar address update, passport status, ration card download, scholarship application - all from your phone via UMANG. No need to take leave from work to visit government offices.
Digital payments everywhere: UPI works at street vendors, autorickshaws, kirana stores. No need to carry cash. Direct bank-to-bank transfer in seconds.

Rural connectivity: BharatNet brings high-speed broadband to villages, enabling online classes, telemedicine consultations with city doctors, and access to digital government services from village CSCs.
Language accessibility: BHASHINI's translation services and UMANG's 23-language support mean you can use digital services in your native language - not just English or Hindi.

how_to_apply.title: Link your mobile to Aadhaar (one-time setup)
how_to_apply.description: Most Digital India services need your Aadhaar-linked mobile for OTP-based authentication. If not yet linked, visit your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC), Aadhaar enrolment centre, or post office with your Aadhaar to update the mobile number.

how_to_apply.title: Download core Digital India apps
how_to_apply.description: From Google Play Store or Apple App Store, download: (a) UMANG - for 2,446 government services in one app, (b) DigiLocker - for digital document storage and verification, (c) BHIM UPI - for digital payments. Verify the official publisher is the Government of India / NIC / MeitY before installing.

how_to_apply.title: Register using OTP
how_to_apply.description: Open each app, enter your Aadhaar-linked mobile number. You receive an OTP for verification. Set a 4-6 digit PIN (MPIN for UMANG / Security PIN for DigiLocker). No documents are uploaded at this stage - only verification.

how_to_apply.title: Start using services in your language
how_to_apply.description: Each app supports multiple Indian languages (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Assamese and others). Select your preferred language from settings. Browse services by department, scheme, or category. Most services give results instantly via Aadhaar-based verification.

important_alert.text: Digital India services (DigiLocker, UMANG, UPI, BHASHINI) are free for citizens. Download apps only from official Play Store / App Store. Beware of scam websites or agents claiming to charge for registration.

faqs.question: What is the Digital India programme?
faqs.answer: Digital India is the Government of India's flagship programme to transform India into a digitally empowered society. Launched on 1 July 2015 by PM Modi, it operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and includes major initiatives like DigiLocker, UMANG, BharatNet, UPI, BHASHINI, and Common Service Centres. It is structured around 9 strategic pillars covering broadband, e-governance, e-services, digital literacy, and electronics manufacturing.

faqs.question: Is Digital India a scheme I can apply for?
faqs.answer: Digital India is not a single scheme with an application form. It is an umbrella programme that delivers digital services to all Indian citizens for free. To benefit, you don't need to apply - you simply use the platforms: download UMANG and DigiLocker from your app store, use UPI through any payment app (BHIM, GooglePay, PhonePe etc.), access BharatNet through your village CSC, or use BHASHINI translation services on supported portals like IRCTC.

faqs.question: How many people use DigiLocker and UMANG in 2026?
faqs.answer: As of 2026: DigiLocker has 67 crore registered users with 967 crore documents issued. UMANG has 10.51 crore registered users and over 741 crore transactions completed. UMANG offers 2,446 government services across 3,543 schemes in 23 Indian languages. These numbers are growing rapidly with new users signing up daily.

faqs.question: Is DigiLocker accepted as legal proof of documents?
faqs.answer: Yes. DigiLocker is legally recognised under the Information Technology Act, 2000. Documents stored or issued via DigiLocker (Aadhaar, PAN, driving licence, vehicle RC, education certificates, COVID vaccination certificate) are accepted as legally valid proof across government offices, banks, schools, hospitals, and traffic police checks. You don't need to carry physical copies.

faqs.question: How does BharatNet help my village?
faqs.answer: BharatNet brings high-speed broadband internet via 6.92 lakh km of optical fibre cable to 2.18 lakh Gram Panchayats across India. This enables: (1) online education for school and college students, (2) telemedicine consultations with city doctors from your village CSC, (3) digital government services through village CSCs without travelling to taluka/district offices, (4) e-commerce and online banking access, (5) WiFi at community spaces in many villages.

faqs.question: What is UPI and how popular is it?
faqs.answer: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is India's flagship real-time digital payment system, run by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It handled 1,867+ crore transactions worth ₹24.77 lakh crore in April 2025 alone, used by 460 million people and 65 million merchants. According to the ACI Worldwide Report 2024, India handled 49% of all global real-time digital transactions in 2023 - making India the global leader. UPI is now live in 7+ countries including UAE, Singapore, France, and Sri Lanka.

faqs.question: What is BHASHINI and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: BHASHINI is the AI-powered language translation platform of the Government of India that breaks language barriers in digital services. It supports 35+ Indian languages with over 1,600 AI models, offering 18 language services including speech-to-text, text-to-speech, translation, OCR, and language detection. BHASHINI is integrated into IRCTC (railway booking), NPCI's IVRS systems, and police documentation. Over 8.5 lakh mobile app downloads. It enables citizens to use digital services in their native language, not just English or Hindi.

faqs.question: What is PMGDISHA and is it still active?
faqs.answer: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) was Digital India's flagship digital literacy programme, training rural adults in basic computer and internet use. It concluded on 31 March 2024 after training 6.39 crore people - exceeding its 6 crore target. While PMGDISHA itself has ended, digital literacy is now part of broader e-governance and CSC training programmes. Common Service Centres continue to offer basic digital training to rural citizens.
